question: Our bookmark button can be selected while it already has another accessibility trait. How would you test what survives toggling its saved state?
Our headings can move after a refresh. Can you strengthen our test so a working rotor doesn't mask a broken ordinary list of headings?
Our contrast checker looks fine with black and white. What unit test would tell us whether intermediate sRGB values give the right luminance?
A row gets reused for another item while someone still holds its old Remove action. How would you check what that old action can actually remove?
Validation is pending when the text field changes directly, without going through our edit helper. Can you test which submission the eventual reply is allowed to accept?
We expose a data grid with a cell spanning several columns. What would you test so querying inside the span is as reliable as querying its starting column?
Our panel has a Close button and its exit can be animated. How would you test when it asks to restore focus and which target it asks for?
The motion preference looks correct at launch. Can you test whether it updates while the screen is already open?
A row has a decorative star beside its title. How would you test that configuring the row restores the intended accessibility settings even if the star was exposed before?
Selecting the same playback speed twice should not restart playback. How would you exercise the installed control and check the change events?
Our delivery choice cell updates its selection cues. Can you test that selecting it doesn't erase other traits already assigned to the cell?
Our Mac row has Open, Save and a supplementary shortcut. How would you prove that the ordinary Save button itself still saves rather than opening the item?
Two Mac results can have the same title and swap positions during refresh. Can you test whether the user's selection follows the same result?
After closing an inspector, the original field is still visible but can refuse first responder. What test would show which eligible control is requested instead?
A selected document sits inside an expanded outline group. How would you test whether reordering its siblings silently drops or moves that selection?
A Mac row displays the correct title even if its selected state is reported incorrectly. What test would distinguish those two outcomes?
On Apple TV our results status normally animates. Can you check that the new status actually appears with Reduce Motion enabled, independently of animation?
The details shortcut works on our TV card. How would you test the ordinary Details button without accidentally testing the shortcut or the Play path instead?
Our Apple TV transition has a duration policy. Can you test that the reduced-motion branch really requests an immediate transition, not merely a short one?
Each TV shelf has a heading and separate episode buttons. Can you test our configuration so the shelf itself doesn't replace its children as one accessible element?
